translation:
Treats injury to the spleen from brooding, with inability to contain the blood, or forgetfulness and palpitations, fright and night sweats, waking without sleeping, or pain in the heart and spleen, liking to lie down and eating little, irregular stools, or heavy and painful limbs, irregular menstruation, red and white vaginal discharge, and similar syndromes.

Renshen (1 qian), Baizhu (1 qian), Fushen (1 qian), Zao Ren (1 qian), Yuanzhi (1 qian), Guishen (1 qian), Huangqi (1 qian), Muxiang (3 fen), Gancao (3 fen).

Cut the above into slices and decoct in water, using three longan-flesh pieces as the guiding agent. The heart stores the spirit and governs the blood; the liver stores the ethereal soul and stores the blood; the spleen stores the intention and commands the blood. If brooding injures them all, the blood does not return to the channels, hence the above syndromes. Treat with this formula to make the qi and blood harmonious and free-flowing, tonify the liver and strengthen the spleen. The blood that has scattered without all returns to the central region and obeys what the greater yin commands.
translator_notes: 歸身 (Guishen) refers to the body portion of Danggui.
中州 (central region) refers to the spleen.
太陰 (greater yin) refers to the spleen.
